question: Should Crabbox support Jujutsu as a first-class repository-state backend, or support only a documented Git-colocation/export bridge?
rationale: The current public synchronization model defines identity and workspace contents through Git, while native Jujutsu support requires product choices about change selection, multiple parents, colocated repositories, remote seeding, and comparison-base semantics.

options.title: First-class Jujutsu backend
options.body: Introduce a VCS-neutral repository-state boundary and implement native Jujutsu discovery with multi-parent integration coverage while preserving existing Git behavior.

options.title: Supported Git bridge
options.body: Document one supported colocated-Git or export workflow and reject ambiguous Jujutsu states with actionable diagnostics.

options.title: Remain Git-only
options.body: Explicitly document Jujutsu as unsupported and require users to supply a conventional Git checkout or fresh-PR source.

recommendation.title: First-class Jujutsu backend
recommendation.body: Introduce a VCS-neutral repository-state boundary and implement native Jujutsu discovery with multi-parent integration coverage while preserving existing Git behavior.
